briefing.text: The bh04 tables (about 34 patients with endometrial or ovarian dMMR/MSI tumours profiled by MSK-IMPACT) may have no explicit best-response or RECIST column. Grep every clinical column header for RESPONSE/BOR/RECIST/CR/PR and confirm that the cohort is gynecologic dMMR (CANCER_TYPE, MSI_TYPE). Under the benchmark convention, if the cohort matches the hypothesis (nivolumab in dMMR gynecologic cancers) but no response column exists, the label must be True or False. Base it on the study's reported finding and established biology, not on 'Not verifiable'. Say which kind of evidence decided the label.
briefing.reason: A missing response variable is the most likely way to end up with a wrong 'Not verifiable' label.

briefing.text: Overall survival, OS_STATUS (% alive) and TMB are not objective response under RECIST 1.1. Do not turn them into a response rate. Use any such proxy only as weak supporting context.
briefing.reason: Without a response column, teams may compute a fake ORR from survival or TMB.

briefing.text: Compute ORR at the patient level. Deduplicate to one row per PATIENT_ID, because a patient can have several samples. Use the all-enrolled (ITT) denominator as primary and the response-evaluable denominator as a sensitivity analysis. The choice of denominator, and whether unconfirmed responses count, can move ORR by several points.
briefing.reason: With a 50% threshold, a few points can flip the comparison.

briefing.text: Enrollment in a dMMR trial is usually by MMR immunohistochemistry. MSIsensor MSI_TYPE (Stable/Indeterminate) can disagree with it, for example because of MLH1 promoter hypermethylation or low purity. Do not drop MSI-Stable/Indeterminate patients from the cohort denominator. Treat discordance as a subgroup analysis only.
briefing.reason: Filtering by MSI_TYPE would quietly change the cohort and the denominator.

briefing.text: Lynch-associated (germline MMR), sporadic MLH1-hypermethylated and POLE-mutant tumours differ in TMB and possibly in response. Subgroup rates can be reported, but the hypothesis is about ORR in the whole cohort. Do not read a subgroup ORR as the cohort ORR.
briefing.reason: This prevents answering the hypothesis with a subgroup figure.

briefing.text: If any response proxy exists, report responders/n with an exact Clopper-Pearson 95% CI and a binomial test against 0.5. With n around 30 the CI spans about ±18 points, so state where the point estimate falls relative to 50% as well as whether the test is significant.
briefing.reason: The hypothesis is a threshold claim on a small cohort, so the inference has to be framed properly.

briefing.text: Background, recalled from memory and not verified: ORRs for PD-1 blockade in dMMR/MSI-H endometrial cancer reported across trials fall roughly in the 40-60% range, which straddles 50% (KEYNOTE-158 about 48-57%, GARNET dostarlimab about 43-45%). A generic class-level prior therefore cannot settle a '<50%' claim. The decision depends on what this specific nivolumab dMMR gynecologic study reported.
briefing.reason: This tells teams that broad biology is ambiguous at this threshold, so they reason about the specific study and do not default to a class prior.

shared_assumptions: Both teams took the study's reported ORR to be above 50% (about 58-59%). Neither checked this against the data. Both figures match the bh04-library recall note (sl-lab-9323d74658cf, 'recall-based; web search unavailable'). So the two teams' agreement may come from one unverified source and is not independent confirmation.
Both assumed the 33 sequenced patients are the cohort the hypothesis is about, and that the ORR in question is the whole-cohort ORR in a single trial.
Both assumed that 'dMMR gynecologic cancers' means the whole enrolled cohort (endometrial plus ovarian), not only the endometrial or IHC-confirmed subset.
unused_evidence: PATIENT_DISPLAY_NAME / SAMPLE_DISPLAY_NAME (manuscript IDs) run up to 36, but only 33 patients are present. IDs 2, 32 and 34 are missing. The enrolled or evaluable trial population is therefore larger than the deposited set. Neither team used this to work out which denominator a reported ORR refers to.

Cancer type detail (30 endometrial vs 3 ovarian, with several histologies) was counted but not used to ask whether the reported ORR is for the whole cohort or an endometrial-only subgroup, which could sit on the other side of 50%.

OS_MONTHS/OS_STATUS, TMB, MSI_SCORE and the mutation/CNA files (e.g. MLH1, MMR genes, POLE) were not used even as context for the published result. This is correct for computing ORR, but it was also not used to check whether the cohort composition matches the recalled trial.
The sample counts the teams report disagree: team-b's memory note says 34 samples, while both method notes say 33/33. This was not reconciled.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A named its weakest point as an unverified recollection of the ORR (~59%), noting class ORRs sit near 50%. It reported this but did not resolve it.

Team B named its weakest point as a recalled ORR (~58%) not based on data. It reported this but did not resolve it. Neither team checked whether its recollection is independent of the library note it was given.
second_readings: 'Patients with dMMR gynecologic cancers' could mean all enrolled patients, all response-evaluable patients, or only the endometrial subgroup. Published ORRs can differ by denominator (intention-to-treat vs evaluable), and a value near 50% can cross the threshold.

'ORR less than 50%' could be read as a point estimate below 50% or as the confidence interval excluding 50%. With n of about 33-36, the CI almost certainly spans 50%. A 'True' could also be argued if the hypothesis is read as a statistical claim that cannot exclude 50%, though the benchmark convention favours the reported point estimate.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed 'False' only moderately. Both teams cite the same ~58-59% figure, which matches a recall-based library note, so their agreement is not independent. Neither team pinned down which denominator or subgroup the figure describes, and the class-level ORR sits close to the 50% threshold.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your label rests on a recalled ORR of ~59%. The library note you received gives ~58% and says it is recall-based. Can you state whether your figure is an independent recollection or comes from that note, and what number of responders over what denominator it implies? Does the label survive if the true figure is a few points lower?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate PATIENT_DISPLAY_NAME. The manuscript IDs run to 36, but 33 patients are present (2, 32 and 34 are absent). What does this imply about the trial's enrolled or evaluable denominator? Does your recalled ORR refer to the enrolled, evaluable or sequenced population, and does that choice move it across 50%?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Split the cohort by CANCER_TYPE (endometrial vs ovarian). Is your recalled ORR the whole-cohort figure or an endometrial-only figure? If the two differ, which one does the hypothesis's 'dMMR gynecologic cancers' refer to, and does that change the label?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your memory note says 34 samples but your method note says 33/33. Recount unique SAMPLE_ID and PATIENT_ID in the sample table and gene panel matrix. Does the corrected count change your cohort description or your MSI discordance count?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your label rests on a recalled ORR of ~58%, the same figure as the recall-based library note. State whether your figure is independent of that note. Tabulate PATIENT_DISPLAY_NAME (IDs run to 36 and 33 are present). Which denominator (enrolled, evaluable or sequenced) does the recalled ORR use, and does the label hold under each?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Split by CANCER_TYPE and CANCER_TYPE_DETAILED. Does the reported ORR you rely on describe the whole gynecologic cohort or the endometrial subgroup? If only a subgroup figure is above 50%, does the whole-cohort reading change your label?

questions.why: The deposited cohort is smaller than the manuscript numbering suggests, and the class ORR sits near 50%. Knowing which denominator convention applies decides whether a reported ORR falls above or below the threshold.

questions.question: What objective response rates have been reported for single-agent nivolumab in mismatch-repair-deficient gynecologic (endometrial and ovarian) cancers, overall and by tumour type?
questions.why: Both teams' labels depend on an unverified recalled figure that may come from a single shared recall note. An independent check is the only way to settle a claim stated against a 50% threshold.

findings.question: In phase II trials of PD-1 inhibitor monotherapy for mismatch-repair-deficient endometrial and ovarian cancers, how are objective response rates usually reported: for all enrolled patients, for response-evaluable patients, or separately by tumour type? How much do these figures typically differ?
findings.answer: Not settled by the web. Every research call failed (HTTP 502: Exa returned HTTP 403), so I read no sources. Unverified general practice: the primary ORR is usually given for response-evaluable patients, often alongside all treated patients and by tumour type. In small cohorts (about 30-40 patients), dropping 2-4 non-evaluable patients moves the ORR by roughly 3-10 points, which is enough to cross a 50% threshold. Treat this as unverified.
